observed_categories.reason: Exfiltrates visited page paths, page domain, and referrer URLs on active browser tabs.
Collects and syncs distinct user identification (userId), device ID parameters, and linked PayPal email attributes.
Captures user items inside shopping carts, quantities, currency types, item images, prices, checkout transaction IDs, and active discounts.

matches.reason: Observed data extraction for page_url_and_referrer maps directly to the external policy declared category user_activity.
Observed data extraction for user_identity_tokens maps directly to the external policy declared category personally_identifiable_information.
Observed data extraction for shopping_cart_details maps directly to the external policy declared category financial_and_payment_information.

overdeclared_external.reason: The external policy covers core PayPal/Honey user account login and credentials, though the extension only uses cached tokens client-side.
Covers member support email correspondences and friends referrals, which are handled on the website rather than extension scripts.
Determines region or locale server-side via IP, which does not require GPS coordinate reads in content scripts.
The policy declares website interactions globally across services, whereas the extension restricts DOM queries to shopping/cart nodes.

developer_statement_checks.reason: The external policy states user data is not sold to third-parties. Static analysis of codebase confirms that telemetry data is sent exclusively to owned Honey/PayPal servers.

overall_assessment.summary: The developer's external privacy policy shows absolute consistency with actual client-side extension behavior. Every observed data extraction flow is fully covered by data categories (Personal Identifiers, Financial Details, User Activity) declared in the statement.

limitations: Static client-side analysis cannot monitor subsequent data brokers transfers or backend data warehousing behaviors.
The external privacy statement is general and covers both joinhoney.com, PayPal, and mobile apps collectively, which accounts for overdeclared categories.
